en: The Philippine archipelago officially consists of 7,641 islands, which is 534 more than the previously taught count of 7,107.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River in Luzon is the longest river in the country, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from its source to its mouth.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Taal Volcano is the second most active volcano in the Philippines and sits entirely within a 300-square-kilometer caldera lake.
The Philippine Trench is the deepest oceanic trench in the country, plunging to a maximum depth of 10,540 meters below sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer underground river that flows directly out into the West Philippine Sea.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of over 3,800 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities in the Philippines.
Palawan is the largest island province in the Philippines by land area, covering approximately 14,649 square kilometers of land.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares of pristine marine habitat in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
The Sierra Madre mountain range is the longest in the Philippines, stretching approximately 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon.
The Philippines is located about 100 kilometers east of Vietnam and roughly 800 kilometers north of the Indonesian island of Borneo.
